key_insight: Medical AI rankings varied by healthcare role and capability, showing why one overall score cannot capture performance across healthcare needs.
clinical_relevance: Context-specific evaluation can inform model selection for healthcare tasks, but these benchmark results do not establish clinical safety or effectiveness.
method: Organized benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities.
Selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction, then added a private diagnostic reasoning benchmark.
Evaluated frontier language models and aggregated results into an overall Index and role- and capability-specific scores.
evidence_signal: Across five benchmarks, overall Index scores ranged from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100; all ten highest-ranked models scored higher on patient communication than clinical decision-making.
watch_item: The Atlas covers only three of nine role–capability cells, limiting conclusions about performance across diverse healthcare needs.
paper_title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
